chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from their forefathers, peace be upon them,

That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he besieged the people of Ta'if, said: 'Any slave who comes out to us before his master is free, and any slave who comes out to us after his master is a slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a slave who escapes to the Muslims during a military campaign?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the status of slaves of polytheists, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) pragmatic legal ruling during the Siege of Ta'if, distinguishing between slaves who fled independently versus those who escaped with their masters. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of manumission (*itq*) as a direct consequence of seeking refuge with the Muslim community, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of liberating those who seek protection under the covenant of Islam.
